title: The 10 Best Digital Calipers
subtitle: 6-inch digital calipers for woodworking, 3D printing, machining and DIY, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A digital caliper measures outside, inside, depth and step dimensions to a thousandth of an inch: bolt diameters, board thickness, 3D-print tolerances and drill bits. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (a stainless steel body, IP54 shop-dust and coolant protection, fraction readout and a data output port). The big divide is material: stainless steel calipers are accurate to about ±0.001 inch, while plastic ones read to ±0.01 inch, ten times coarser. They run from about $9 for Adoric's plastic caliper to $140 for Starrett's.

buyers_guide.a: Stainless steel calipers are accurate to about ±0.001 inch and hold up for years. Plastic calipers read to ±0.01 inch, ten times coarser, and the jaws flex. Plastic is fine for rough measuring; anything with tolerances needs steel.

Resolution is the smallest step the display shows (0.0005 inch on good calipers). Accuracy is how close the reading is to the truth (typically ±0.001 inch). A display can show more digits than the caliper can actually measure.
IP54 calipers resist dust and splashing water or coolant. Unsealed digital calipers can glitch when dust or moisture gets into the electronics.
If you work in fractional inches (woodworking, drill bits), a fraction mode saves converting decimals. Machinists usually prefer decimal inches or millimeters.

buyers_guide.q: How do I get accurate readings?
buyers_guide.a: Clean the jaws, close them and zero before measuring, use light consistent pressure, and measure square to the part. Replace the battery when the display flickers or drifts.
